I agree that blanket GenAI bans won't be viable much longer, as competition will move much faster.

But also, game development economics are very different from SaaS products. You can't spend a ton of money in tokens per month and expect that the gains from selling those features will support the cost of building them. Game dev margins are already slim-to-negative for most independent studios.

children.author: liljacob
children.text:
For a game that values quantity I would agree, but in a sense, games are often sort of like a piece of art, and something hand crafted will always resonate with people more than something that was mass produced in a factory.

So for mobile games, sports franchises, generic shooters etc. using AI would probably not affect sales or success. But for something where immersion and gameplay quality is the focus, hand coding will be the way to go.

Where creativity doesn’t matter, such as with QA and security, AI will still speed things up considerably without compromising the integrity of the content.

children.author: bob1029
children.text:
Contemporary AI is not very good at the parts of game dev that are genuinely difficult.

It is fantastic at the code. Monobehaviors are completely solved. I ~never have to look at c# code or shaders again if I choose not to. However, this was like 5% of the problem.

Composing a three-dimensional scene graph in a way that is compelling to a human observer is not something an LLM will ever be very competent at. I worry about those who are in the midst of conflating the capabilities of diffusion models with those of "world" models. The former make it seem as if we are "so close". The latter are more or less non-existent.

I understand the sentiment, but I feel like not using AI for game dev isn’t going to be economically viable much longer, and I wonder why companies don’t just embrace it while it still gives them an edge.

children.author: bearjaws
children.text:
Gamers have to be one of the most interesting groups of people. I'll define "gamers" as people who spend more than 40 hours a week playing games, and probably overlaps significantly with streamer consumption.

Extremely needy, demanding, and simultaneously spineless.

Riot releases a $500 skin and make a million dollars, GTA6 has a $400 edition that doesn't include the game, and of course the OG horse armor.

Outrage after outrage, yet they keep on buying.

Additionally, 99% of them have no clue how hard it is to build a game, at any scale really. They don't understand where corners have been cut, and that it's possible to use AI without cutting corners.

They quite literally demand the world despite having never created a single thing themselves, blindly consuming, never producing.

Personally, it makes no sense to build a game without AI. A lot of code is needed and you need to iterate on it, perfect use case for AI.

Art, buttons, sprites, and models, often need rounds of iteration, why not start with a basic set and work on it?

There's nothing wrong with iterating, there is plenty wrong with slop. So let's be mad at the slop, not the AI itself.
